extracted.intended_audience: general public, journalists, researchers, and others interested in Hollywood labor disputes and the 2023 WGA strike
extracted.subtask_description: A factual, encyclopedic summary of the 2023 Writers Guild of America strike: causes, demands, timeline, negotiation positions, strike rules, impacts on productions, and outcomes. Geared to readers seeking an overview and reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: WGA member strike conduct rules
rubrics_metrics.description: "writers cannot do any writing, revising, pitching, or discussing future projects with companies that are members of the AMPTP."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Guild set prospective rules for writers during the strike: forbidding writing, revising, pitching, or discussing future projects for AMPTP-member companies; fiction podcasts produced by companies against which the Guild is striking must stop production; the Guild noted it cannot punish non-Guild writers but may bar such writers from future Guild membership. The WGA also instructed members to begin picketing at set times and provided Q&A guidance (e.g., for Animation Guild-covered writers) about whether particular work would be counter to strike activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streaming residuals / compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Residuals from streaming media were a principal point of disagreement; the WGA claimed the AMPTP's share of such residuals had cut much of writers' average incomes compared to a decade prior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The WGA estimated its proposals would yield writers about US$429 million a year, whereas the AMPTP's offer would yield about $86 million. The dispute included calls for success-based residual payments from streaming services and other reforms to how streaming work is compensated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on generative artificial intelligence (genAI)
rubrics_metrics.description: WGA demanded strict limits on generative AI and that the Agreement state genAI would not be used to replace writers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The union sought regulation prohibiting exploitation of writers' material to train AI models, produce digital recreations, or enable efforts to use AI to reduce writers or their pay. The AMPTP later presented its own proposal suggesting rules for AI content (Aug 22, 2023); studios indicated limited willingness to discuss safeguards but resisted some WGA proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory staffing and duration of employment
rubrics_metrics.description: Guild proposal for 'mandatory staffing' and 'duration of employment' — requiring all shows to be staffed with a minimum number of writers for a minimum amount of time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WGA wanted terms to be added to the contract that would require specified staffing minimums and guaranteed employment periods ("whether needed or not" per AMPTP). AMPTP described these as primary sticking points; studios resisted mandatory staffing guarantees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual pension and health fund entitlement
rubrics_metrics.description: WGA advocated ensuring each member of a writing team receives their own pension and their own health care funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AMPTP rejected the proposal and did not offer a counterproposal; a tentative agreement later included shifting 0.5% of negotiated minimums for all WGA minimums into pensions and health funds as a concession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum Basic Agreement (MBA) coverage distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: The MBA established minimum wages for television and film writers but historically applied to broadcast television and not to streaming television.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This coverage distinction meant writers on streaming-produced shows were often not covered by the MBA and had to negotiate individually with streaming companies, contributing to pay disparities. The MBA expired on May 1, 2023, preceding the strike.

rubrics_metrics.name: WGA core goals summarized
rubrics_metrics.description: Infobox-stated goals: Increase funding and job security for writers; increase the size of writers' rooms; limit the use of artificial intelligence in the writing process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These succinct goals guided the union's negotiating positions and public messaging throughout the strike, framing demands on compensation (including streaming residuals), staffing, pensions/health, and AI protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guild enforcement and solidarity guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for picketing, solidarity actions, and support mechanisms during the strike.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The WGA instructed picketing at particular locations and times, coordinated with other unions (e.g., SAG-AFTRA, Teamsters, Animation Guild) on solidarity actions, advised writers facing financial hardship to apply to the Entertainment Community Fund, and communicated potential membership consequences for crossing strike rules. Some allied unions issued Q&A documents to help members determine how to honor picket lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Studios' counter-strategies and positions (AMPTP)
rubrics_metrics.description: AMPTP/studios' positions included limited concessions on AI safeguards but resistance to WGA staffing/duration and success-based streaming residuals; studios planned tactics to endure a prolonged strike.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article reports studio executives planned to delay negotiations and use available content libraries and completed productions to lessen impact; AMPTP presented its own AI-content proposal and framed WGA staffing demands as unrealistic. These opposing criteria shaped negotiation dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisions in tentative agreement as measures of success
rubrics_metrics.description: Outcomes the WGA cited as wins in the tentative agreement: increases to minimum wage, final compensation, pension and health fund rates; improvements to length-of-employment and writing team size terms; increases to residual payments for domestic and foreign streaming works; regulation of AI to prohibit exploitation of writers' material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These specific contractual changes were used to justify ratification (99% approval) and are presented as the practical standards by which the strike's success was evaluated by the union and commentators.
